title: Depth reduced the BATS thickness-model AOU error, but an excess remained on sigma-theta 26.5 in 2019-2025
abstract: At BATS, we tested whether density-class thickness gives information about apparent oxygen utilization (AOU) beyond the depth of sigma-theta 26.5. We rebuilt annual profiles from BCO-DMO bottle data for 1989-2025. Models fitted in 1989-2009 used measured geometry to estimate AOU in 2010-2025. Adding depth to thickness reduced test RMSE from 5.18 to 4.00 umol/kg. The 2019-2025 mean excess fell from 5.08 to 3.25 umol/kg but remained positive, with a refit block interval of 0.31 to 7.08. Moving the surface through a fixed monthly oxygen profile gave 46% of the 11.65 umol/kg long-term AOU rise. Thickness kept a negative relation to AOU in annual differences after depth was included. Last year's geometry did not improve one-year forecasts over AR(1) or persistence. These results support thickness as a same-year indicator but do not identify respiration or ventilation rates. The study is exploratory, uses sparse bottles at one site, and cannot validate the denser surfaces with strict interpolation. Code, annual results, source hashes and an independent numerical audit are included.

display.caption: BATS on sigma-theta 26.5: same-year models, fixed-profile counterfactual, remaining error and one-year forecasts. Models use training years 1989-2009. The primary profile gap limit is 250 m.

citations.reason: We test its class-thickness relation with depth controls, new bottle processing, a fixed-profile counterfactual and advance forecasts. The remaining excess depends on profile processing.
